review_note: The source derives product decomposition R≅R1×R2 from an open disjoint decomposition of Spec(R), and requires each factor to be both a quotient and a localization. The draft's expanded spectral projection maps agree with the previously reviewed product-spectrum lemma.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring.
If $\Spec(R) = U \amalg V$ with both $U$ and $V$ open
then $R \cong R_1 \times R_2$ with $U \cong \Spec(R_1)$
and $V \cong \Spec(R_2)$ via the maps on spectra induced by the two projection ring homomorphisms $R\to R_1$ and $R\to R_2$.
Moreover, both $R_1$ and $R_2$ are localizations as well as quotients
of the ring $R$.
conclusions:

of the ring $R$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-disjoint-implies-product}
Let $R$ be a ring.
If $\Spec(R) = U \amalg V$ with both $U$ and $V$ open
then $R \cong R_1 \times R_2$ with $U \cong \Spec(R_1)$
and $V \cong \Spec(R_2)$ via the maps in Lemma \ref{lemma-spec-product}.
Moreover, both $R_1$ and $R_2$ are localizations as well as quotients
of the ring $R$.

review_note: Preserves the exact biconditional: injectivity of canonical M→⊕_i M_{fi} versus injectivity of m↦(f1m,…,fnm) into a finite direct sum of M. No covering hypothesis on the fi was introduced.
statement:
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in R$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Then $M \to \bigoplus M_{f_i}$ is injective if and only if
$$
M \longrightarrow \bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} M, \quad
m \longmapsto (f_1m, \ldots, f_nm)
$$
is injective.

\label{lemma-when-injective-covering}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in R$.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module.
Then $M \to \bigoplus M_{f_i}$ is injective if and only if
$$
M \longrightarrow \bigoplus\nolimits_{i = 1, \ldots, n} M, \quad
m \longmapsto (f_1m, \ldots, f_nm)
